title: Valence-Driven Structural Transformation and Phase Coexistence in Chemically Substituted EuPd2Si2
authors: Masoud Mardani, Shivani Sharma, Saul H. Lapidus, Theo Siegrist
abstract: EuPd2Si2 serves as an ideal system to probe the interplay between lattice dynamics and electronic instabilities through its tunable valence transition, responsive to temperature, pressure, and magnetic field. Here, we focus on investigating the origin of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in pristine EuPd2Si2, alloyed EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05, and EuPd2Si1.9Ge0.1 and its correlation with structural responses. Compared with the parent compound EuPd2Si2 which exhibits the europium valence transition at Tv = 143 K, magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal a systematic shift in Tv with Ge substitution, decreasing to 87 K for EuPd2Si1.95Ge0.05. Temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction confirms phase coexistence between Eu2+Pd2Si2-xGex and Eu3+Pd2Si2-xGex phases across the valence transition for all samples measured (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10). The pronounced increase in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) well above Tv reflects the gradual nature of the transformation and highlights the role of structural strain in stabilizing the coexisting phases, supporting the presence of a phase-segregated ground state, in contrast to a homogeneous intermediate-valence or mixed-valence state. The variation in Tv across different compositions correlates with changes in lattice parameters, highlighting the robust coupling between the structural and electronic degrees of freedom. The phase diagram suggests an inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and Tv, suggesting a possible predictive framework for estimating transition temperatures in other chemically substituted variants of this family.
summary: This work uses synchrotron X-ray diffraction and magnetic measurements to study the valence transition in $	ext{EuPd}_2	ext{Si}_2$ and its Ge-substituted analogs. The key finding is that the transition involves structural phase coexistence between $	ext{Eu}^{2+}$ and $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$ phases. The study establishes a quantitative, inverse linear relationship between the lattice parameter and the transition temperature, providing a predictive framework for related materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin and structural consequences of the temperature-induced europium valence instability in $	ext{EuPd}_2	ext{Si}_2$ and its chemically substituted variants.
main_result: The valence transition is confirmed to be associated with structural phase coexistence between $	ext{Eu}^{2+}$ and $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$ phases, suggesting a phase-segregated ground state rather than a homogeneous mixed-valence state.
method: The research employed temperature-dependent synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) and magnetic susceptibility measurements on polycrystalline samples.
model_or_system: The system is the intermetallic compound $	ext{EuPd}_2	ext{Si}_2$ and its solid solutions formed by substituting Si with Ge ($	ext{EuPd}_2	ext{Si}_{2-x}	ext{Ge}_x$). The focus is on the interplay between electronic valence state ($	ext{Eu}^{2+}$ vs $	ext{Eu}^{3+}$) and lattice structure.
key_observables: Transition temperature ($T_v$), lattice parameters ($a, c$), XRD peak splitting/broadening, Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM), and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$).
important_parameters: Temperature (T), Ge substitution concentration ($x$), and lattice parameter ($a$).
main_assumptions: The structural changes observed at low temperatures are attributed to the valence instability rather than standard thermal contraction, and an empirical linear relationship between $T_v$ and lattice parameter is proposed.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structure, the systematic shift of $T_v$ with Ge substitution, and the correlation between lattice parameters and $T_v$ via linear fitting.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the structural and magnetic data across different Ge concentrations, confirming phase coexistence via XRD peak splitting and establishing an empirical relationship between the lattice parameter and the transition temperature.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between electronic valence changes and measurable structural parameters (lattice constants, phase coexistence) provides a concrete example of how electronic correlations manifest macroscopically in the solid state.
